EU fines chatbot maker over training data

Published 2026-10-07 06:30 UTC

A European data protection authority has fined a chatbot developer 15 million euros after concluding that the company scraped personal information from public websites to train its language models without a valid legal basis under the General Data Protection Regulation.

The regulator said the company collected names, photos, contact details and forum posts from millions of people, many of them in the EU, and kept the material in training datasets long after it was needed. Investigators also found that the company's privacy notice did not tell people their data was being used to build an AI product, and that requests to delete personal data were answered with form letters rather than action.

The decision orders the developer to stop processing the scraped data within six months, to delete records it cannot justify keeping, and to run an awareness campaign explaining how people can object. The company must also give the authority a written plan describing how it will filter personal data out of future training runs.

The company said it disagreed with the decision and would appeal. In a statement, it argued that training on publicly available text serves a legitimate interest and that its models do not memorize information about individuals. It said it had already introduced an opt-out form and had removed some sources from its datasets.

Privacy advocates welcomed the fine but said the amount was small compared with what large AI companies spend on computing. They want regulators to require model retraining when unlawfully collected data is found, rather than allowing companies to keep models built on that data.

The case is the latest in a series of European actions against AI developers. Several other national regulators have open investigations into how chatbots handle personal information, and the European Data Protection Board is preparing guidance on when web scraping for model training can be lawful. Lawyers expect the appeal to take at least a year.
